raw_title: Royal Enfield Flying Flea Reaches Chennai, 14 Outlets Planned
title: Royal Enfield Flying Flea Reaches Chennai, 14 Outlets Planned
raw_summary: GaadiWaadi - The electric motorcycle brand will establish 14 sales and service touchpoints in Chennai taking its planned Indian retail network to 40 locations in four cities Royal Enfield has extended the availability of its Flying Flea C6 electric motorcycle to Chennai where 14 new sales and service touchpoints are planned. The city becomes the fourth Indian market for Flying Flea following Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Pune. The Chennai network will have two company operated stores and 12 partner outlets providing customers more locations to inspect the motorcycle, arrange test rides and access after-sales assistance. The dedicated Flying Flea stores will operate at OMR and Adyar while the remaining outlets will function alongside existing Royal Enfield dealerships. The locations are situated in areas such as Anna Nagar, Tambaram, Pallikaranai, Avadi, Tondiarpet and Nandanam. Royal Enfield has also identified 11 service centres in Chennai for routine maintenance and technical assistance. These centres will support the C6 as retail operations commence in the city. The brand already has 12 sales and service locations in Bengaluru, four in Hyderabad, and 10 in Pune. Chennai’s 14 new touchpoints will increase the planned network to 40 locations nationwide. Pune received its 10-centre network in late October, shortly before the Chennai announcement. The combination of dedicated showrooms and established Royal Enfield dealerships provides Flying Flea a retail presence in different parts of each city. The Flying Flea C6 costs Rs. 2.79 lakh while the Battery-as-a-Service option reduces the initial motorcycle price to Rs. 1.99 lakh (both prices, ex-showroom). The latter arrangement separates the battery cost from the initial vehicle purchase and requires a subscription payment. The upfront difference stands at Rs. 80,000 but the subscription charges must also be considered when comparing ownership costs. The motorcycle is available in Storm Black, Flea Green, and Parachute White. The C6 has a distinctive design inspired by the lightweight Royal Enfield Flying Flea motorcycles of the 1940s. A circular LED headlamp, slim upper bodywork, exposed forged-aluminium frame, and aluminium girder front fork distinguish it from other electric motorcycles. The compact battery assembly sits inside a magnesium enclosure beneath the tank-like upper section. The narrow rear bodywork, exposed structural components and lightweight styling also separate the C6 visually from the traditional Royal Enfield motorcycles. The electric motorcycle uses a 3.91 kWh battery and a permanent-magnet synchronous motor producing around 20.7 hp and 60 Nm of torque. Royal Enfield claims a maximum speed of 115 kmph and a riding range of 154 km under the Indian Driving Cycle. The electronics comprise five riding modes, traction control and lean-sensitive ABS. The C6 also has connected functions, smartphone integration and configurable electronic responses. Flying Flea is preparing a second electric motorcycle, the S6 scrambler, for a summer 2027 launch. Revealed at EICMA 2026, the S6 uses wire-spoke wheels, block-pattern tyres, an enduro-style seat, and a dedicated off-road riding mode. The scrambler shares its underlying architecture with the road-biased C6 but has different equipment for recreational trail riding.

raw_title: How Can Europe Accelerate Electric Trucking?
title: How Can Europe Accelerate Electric Trucking?
raw_summary: Europe is having a hard time lately, with skyrocketing oil prices dampening economies. Fuel costs, particularly diesel, are prompting surging interest in truck electrification. Europe has been urging truck makers to move toward electric trucking, and they have responded with a variety of electric semi trucks from many manufacturers. Europe is a group of sovereign countries with many standards. The European Union is a political and economic union of 27 states in that area. It issued directives urging action and imposing penalties. In response to European Union directives, companies have formed EV100, a coalition of corporations responding to the need. In a recent story, Steve Hanley wrote about European electric truck makers’ difficulties expanding truck electrification . Here’s a quotation from the story: “ In a letter to EU Commission president Ursula von der Leyen, of primary concern, in their estimation, is expanding the charging infrastructure for heavy-duty trucks in Europe.” There is no shortage of electric trucks in Europe. Expansion could go faster were it not for charging infrastructure. Manufacturers complain about “an alarming delay” in conditions needed to drive market uptake. For Europe, truck electrification is not working as well as in China, where over 90% of the world’s electric trucks reside. The differences between China and the EU show some reasons why truck electrification is slower in Europe. How did China succeed where the EU failed? China made electric trucks a freight system, not a vehicle category . Power is a major factor in electric grid infrastructure. Charging electric trucks places demands on power. Peak power determines how much infrastructure is necessary. In grid planning, peak annual power determines how much capital equipment is necessary. Reducing peak power demand is a critical factor for electric truck infrastructure. Figure 1 shows one method of reducing power called route stuffing. It schedules departures on heavy traffic corridors at regularly spaced intervals. Corridors like ones between ports and warehouses are a target for those practices. These corridors often route trucks in a round trip chain. Filling routes with scheduled trips can reduce power demand compared to random trip scheduling. The article Battery Swap Uses Fewer Batteries Than You Think is devoted to methods of analysis and planning that can lead to lower peak power demand. There are other benefits to planning, such as greater truck load capacity from the same amount of batteries. Part of the solution to slow electric truck infrastructure development is to plan infrastructure and truck use practices to reduce the charging power burden. Given the pressing and enduring need due to the diesel fuel cost crisis, it is necessary to reprioritize grid power upgrade demands. Demands for data center power upgrades like transformers for substations should be re shuffled and prioritized toward the diesel crisis.

Figure 1 shows one method of reducing power called route stuffing. It schedules departures on heavy traffic corridors at regularly spaced intervals. Corridors like ones between ports and warehouses are a target for those practices. These corridors often route trucks in a round trip chain. Filling routes with scheduled trips can reduce power demand compared to random trip scheduling. The article Battery Swap Uses Fewer Batteries Than You Think is devoted to methods of analysis and planning that can lead to lower peak power demand. There are other benefits to planning, such as greater truck load capacity from the same amount of batteries. Part of the solution to slow electric truck infrastructure development is to plan infrastructure and truck use practices to reduce the charging power burden. Given the pressing and enduring need due to the diesel fuel cost crisis, it is necessary to reprioritize grid power upgrade demands. Demands for data center power upgrades like transformers for substations should be re shuffled and prioritized toward the diesel crisis.

In two articles, Michael Barnard outlined the issues. Vehicles are not a transportation system. What does Europe have now? It has an EU Commission interacting with a coalition, EV100. The problem is, there are plenty of trucks available, but who is in charge of infrastructure? You can’t have electric trucks without means of charging, but as the coalition complains, “Significant improvements to charging infrastructure, a reduction in carbon dioxide based tolls, and a coherent policy framework are urgently needed.” There are so many stakeholders — including the commission, vehicles makers, and charging companies across multiple countries — that no one is in charge of infrastructure, and without it, nothing moves. It needs a unity of purpose and action.

If China is succeeding, why not adopt its strategy? Perhaps the answer is right in front of everyone’s nose. As Michael puts it, “the policy connects vehicles to corridors, depots, service areas, grids and freight use cases instead of treating sales targets as sufficient.” CATL offered Europe a system, not a vehicle. This is a “turn key” solution. It’s a well thought out system, including use of methods and practices, not an anything goes free-for-all. That kind of stability and predictability is what EV100 leaders are looking for. This is not a swap-or-nothing scenario. Different techniques apply to various use cases. Swap must be planned for high-use freight corridors and other proper applications. Swap trucks can also fast charge or slow charge, providing flexibility and a system of trucks that includes smaller trucks, not just semis.

What does all this have to do with Europe’s slowly advancing infrastructure? Simply put, electric trucks put heavy charging demands on the grid. Trucks can have megawatt-hour batteries that require megawatt power charging to charge in an hour. Reducing grid power demands can reduce grid infrastructure upgrade costs, and leverage capital investment toward faster implementation.

“The process of getting megawatt charging equipment connected to the grid can take several years, delaying deployment even where operators and infrastructure providers are ready to invest.” The need for megawatt charging equipment is reduced by accelerating swap network development instead of fixed battery trucks that must be charged by fast chargers. “ Swaptopus is easy to misread as a quirky name for another electric-truck infrastructure project. It is a newly formed joint venture between Octopus Energy and CATL, created to develop automated battery-swapping hubs for heavy trucks across Europe.” Unlike the government of China that played a role in encouraging standards and cooperation in infrastructure, Europe has a looser arrangement between many countries with various standards. Europe is learning the slow, hard way where battery swapping is most needed .

Every truck application has different optimization. It means that there must be different approaches to fit freight operations in heavy traffic corridors. Quoting Michael Barnard, “Freight operators often run repeated routes between ports, factories, distribution centres and logistics hubs. Those patterns provide known traffic, known stopping points and relatively predictable electricity demand. A swap hub can be placed around an existing freight flow instead of hoping that enough unrelated trucks eventually pass through.”

Freight corridors are a scenario made to order for battery swap. Real trucking solutions include a mix of vehicle and infrastructure types — from small, local delivery, to large, long-haul freight; and from slow, overnight charging, to medium power charging and battery swap — all used in concert to accelerate heavy truck electrification. With a wide variety of charging options, and vehicles and charging use cases targeted in coordination to avoid peak power demands, the path forward is eased. School buses don’t need expensive high-power fast charging. Lower-power chargers can do the trick. Local delivery can use a mix of overnight and medium power charging. Heavy truck dispatch must be more carefully coordinated to avoid peak demand and grid upgrade costs. A mix of medium-power charging and swap stations along with planned use cases can successfully lower electric freight power needs and transport system capital expenses to speed transport electrification.

Everything Electric was a good opportunity to measure public reaction to the new product. Nick tells me that hundreds of people checked out their stall. “People care about carbon cost and comfort. People don’t compromise on comfort.” Sounds like comfort trumps carbon cost. Homeowners who visited the stand and filled out the survey were focused on sustainability and cost. Nick cautions: “it was an electrification expo crowd, and 50 of the 62 already had solar, so it’s not the whole market.” See the chart below.

Although I live in the warmer part of Australia (Brisbane), many Aussies have to endure cold winters. Nick tells me he is looking at installs in Sydney, Canberra, and Melbourne in the deep south. Thermal Dawn can store heat up to 70 degrees Celsius, or down to 5 degrees. Thermal Dawns’ equipment can run cold or hot water through pipes and radiators that are already installed, depending on the need — without having to run an expensive gas boiler. He describes it as a thermal battery. Just to be clear, it does not generate electricity.

Check out this graph below, which shows the Thermal Dawn system in action at a house in Melbourne during a day in August 2026. It shows room temperature and when the heat pump was running, in 15-minute samples, unedited. The heat pump ran until about 1:45pm, then not again, heated by stored energy through the evening peak.

“What about return on investment,” I asked. He described two systems they have had running over the southern Australian winter which have saved the homeowners approximately AU$1,500 each. “The first was a house in Melbourne, our first install, live since May 2026. The owners charge the system in their retailer’s free three-hour midday window, so the heat for the evening costs them close to nothing. The second was a Warragul (slab-heated home, Victoria): installed in two days in July 2026. Our controls turn the home’s concrete slab into part of the battery, managing when it charges and when it releases heat. On 95% of winter evenings, the heat pumps did not run at all between 5 pm and 9pm. Since commissioning, 70,521 MJ of gas has been avoided by just these two installations.”

Nick further explains: “A standard heat pump draws from the grid during those expensive morning and evening hours. You’ve escaped gas, but you’re still paying premium rates every time the temperature drops at night. Thermal Dawn is different. Our system charges when power is cheapest, a free midday window, your own solar, or late-night off-peak, then delivers that stored warmth through your radiators and underfloor heating all evening, with the compressor off through the expensive hours.

It appears that Thermal Dawn’s secret sauce is “Phase Change Materials.” Naturally, Nick declined to share exactly what Thermal Dawn is using. The system replaces a gas boiler with a combination of reverse cycle heat pump, well insulated water tank, and phase change materials. PCMs are designed to freeze or melt at a specific temperature, storing and releasing heat when they change physical state, usually from solid to liquid. “PCM doubles our heat capacity.” The heating applications I could understand, what about the cooling? “Cool water from the tank runs through a fan coil unit, and the fan blows cool air into the room. Cooling is an optional add-on.” That’s the answer.

How do thermal storage and a home battery/solar system work together? “Thermal storage is cheap storage doing one job very well. Heating, cooling, and hot water are the largest, most predictable loads in the house, and covering them thermally is far cheaper per kWh than covering them from lithium. A battery is expensive storage doing a general-purpose job.

raw_summary: Guangzhou, China — XPENG (NYSE: XPEV, HKEX: 9868), a leading Physical AI company, has supported the development of GroundingPI, an open-source visual perception foundation model created by researchers affiliated with XPENG, Peking University, The University of Hong Kong and other academic institutions. article_paragraphs: Guangzhou, China — XPENG (NYSE: XPEV, HKEX: 9868), a leading Physical AI company, has supported the development of GroundingPI, an open-source visual perception foundation model created by researchers affiliated with XPENG, Peking University, The University of Hong Kong and other academic institutions.

The research explores a new approach to embodied intelligence by focusing on a fundamental capability: enabling AI systems to accurately identify objects and understand their spatial positions in the physical world. With approximately 4 billion parameters, GroundingPI achieved the highest aggregate score among 44 baseline models evaluated across 34 perception benchmarks covering 11 capability categories.
The research paper, model weights and supporting code have been made publicly available, enabling researchers and developers to further explore perception-focused approaches to Physical AI.
As AI increasingly moves beyond digital environments into physical applications such as robotics and autonomous driving, accurately understanding the surrounding environment becomes essential.

While general-purpose foundation models have demonstrated strong capabilities in language understanding, reasoning and planning, physical intelligence requires more precise visual perception. AI systems must not only recognize objects but also identify their exact locations and spatial relationships to support real-world interaction.

GroundingPI takes a perception-focused approach to this challenge. Rather than relying on robot action labels during the perceptual model’s training, the research focuses on developing foundational visual understanding capabilities that can support downstream action-learning systems.

For example, when instructed to identify “the handle of the cup on the right”, an AI system needs to locate not only the correct cup but also the precise position of its handle. GroundingPI is designed to represent such information using spatial coordinates, including points and bounding boxes.

The model is trained across 11 categories of perceptual capabilities, including object detection, dense object localization, referring expression grounding, optical character recognition (OCR), document layout understanding, user interface element recognition and robotic spatial localization.

Wheels are orange coloured, which add contrast and ensure a more dynamic presence. Black-finished surfaces utilize a mix of matte black and glossy black. Distinctive graphics have been used in black and orange shades. The scooter uses a single piece seat with a stepped design. The model showcased can be seen with a rack and top box. TVS M1-S has relatively modest specifications and does not appear to be part of the race for higher range and top speed. The focus could be more on accessibility, practical applications, reliability, durability and easy maintenance. The scooter is equipped with a 4.2 kWh lithium-ion NMC battery pack, offering a range of around 120 km (European WMTC testing standards).

The battery is installed in the floorboard, ensuring a low centre of gravity and optimized weight distribution. TVS M1-S uses a permanent magnet synchronous electric motor, bolted on the chassis. It generates 12.5 kW or approximately 17 PS. Continuous output is rated at 5 kW or 6.80 PS. The scooter has a top speed of 105 km/h.

Boles Manufacturing was founded in Burbank, California, in 1946 – the company built a popular line of aluminum travel trailers for 34 years, and it had all started out with a single trailer built in a one-car garage. The Boles Aero never reached Airstream’s national popularity , but their polished aluminum trailers developed a cult following all their own.

Boles Manufacturing was founded in Burbank, California, in 1946 – the company built a popular line of aluminum travel trailers for 34 years, and it had all started out with a single trailer built in a one-car garage. Image courtesy of Boles Aero.
The company was founded by Don and Jeanette Boles, and their built their trailers using methods Don had learned making aircraft.

In 1939, Don Boles was one of the first 37 candidates picked for a new four-year tool and die apprenticeship. The US Department of Labor had set it up as part of the Roosevelt administration’s plan to pull the country out of the Great Depression. It was an interesting time in world history, WWII kicked off that same year across the Atlantic, and two years later the United States would join the conflict after the attack on Pearl Harbor.

Boles served it at Lockheed’s aircraft plant in Burbank, learning aircraft design and construction methods, and he went on to win several awards for tools he designed to improve the way aluminum parts were made. He graduated as a journeyman tool and die maker in 1943, right in the midst of WWII when men with his skillset were in huge demand.

After a short assignment with General Electric in Cleveland, Ohio, Boles enlisted in the U.S. Navy and was posted to a base at Norman, Oklahoma. No housing could be found there for his wife, Jeanette, and their three children, so he bought a used 27 foot trailer, and the family lived in it for the rest of his military service. The couple had met at Burbank High School and married a month after she graduated, when she was 16 and he was 18.

Everyone knows that electric cars are much more inconvenient than gas cars. After all, there is a gas station on every corner and it only takes 5 minutes to fill up. Electric chargers are rare, and it takes at least an hour to charge.
Wrong: If you have access to 220 volt electricity or a L2 charger at home or work, an electric vehicle is much more convenient than a gas car for 300 miles per day of local driving.
In principal: In the evening, you drive into your garage, carport or driveway and take 10 seconds to plug in, the next morning, you have a full charge and take 10 seconds to unplug.

Compare that with a gas car. You probably have to make a couple of special trips per week to the gas station, put in your credit card, grab the smelly nozzle, put it in your car, and wait five minutes to fill. Then you return the smelly nozzle to the pump.
With the gas car, every 3,000 miles, you need to go to a Jiffy Lube and sit in their smelly waiting room for an hour while they change your oil.
With the gas car, every year, you need to go to an inspection station and wait an hour in their smelly waiting room while they do an emissions check.
These three tasks are all eliminated with an electric vehicle, which makes it much more convenient for local driving.

Only the huge political contributions to Trump by the fossil fuel industry and his resulting anti-EV policies have slowed down adoption in this country.

In places we’ve been like California; Portland, Oregon; and northern Utah, you are seeing a lot of Teslas, so you know that electric cars are working for a lot of people these days. It’s time for you to do some research on electric cars.

You do pay a premium for new electric cars, because the batteries are still quite expensive. If price is the driving factor for you, buy a used electric car. Hardly any used EVs are high mileage, and EV batteries still have plenty of life even after they go off warranty at 8 years and 120,000 miles. There are thousands of lightly used EVs sitting at used car lots at reasonable prices all over the country these days. Some used car dealers will give you an estimate of the battery life. If not, get a friend who is an experienced EV driver to help you evaluate the battery life of the EV you are considering.

If you just do local driving or have two cars and have a garage or off-street parking, an EV is a no brainer. EVs are hands-down more convenient than gas cars for local driving. Your EV will have plenty of range for local driving, it will get a complete charge overnight in your home garage refueling station and it will never need an oil change.

EVs are as quiet as mice, as smooth as kittens, and as quick as jackrabbits. They have simple electric motors, not complex internal combustion engines. They have simple one-speed transmissions, not complex 7-speed automatic transmissions. They don’t have exhaust systems with mufflers that will rust and need replacement. They don’t have emission control systems with limited life. They don’t have complex cooling systems with big radiators. You seldom use your brakes with an EV, so your brakes may last the life of the car. They don’t have a big lead-acid battery for starting, with a maximum life of 5 years. New EVs have only a small lithium-ion battery, which lasts 10+ years. Bottom line: Routine maintenance for EVs is almost nil. I think the only real maintenance item on a Tesla over the first 3 years is the cabin air filter. You can expect an EV to go 500,000 miles without major repair or replacement in most cases.

Perhaps you can stomach buying a car from Tesla whose CEO has become one of the most despicable persons on the planet lately. (Example: Musk recently suspended access to his Starlink communications system to the Ukrainians who are valiantly defending their country from the Russian aggressors.) However, Tesla has sold almost 10 million automobiles worldwide that don’t emit CO2 and particulate pollution while operating. Tesla also has by far the most ubiquitous charging system, which allows cross-country driving on major US roads with little planning. Consider buying a Tesla.

So, what about cross-country trips? Everyone knows that long-distance trips in an electric car are inconvenient or even impossible, because there aren’t enough charging stations and it takes an hour if you can find one. Wrong: Every 100 miles along all the major Interstate highways, Tesla has built Superchargers with 8 to 32 and a few with over 100 charging stalls. By the time you have gone to the bathroom, walked the dog, and chatted with a fellow EV owner for a few minutes, you probably have more than enough charge to continue your journey. Usually, charging takes about 20 minutes. If you need a longer charge, you may need to watch a bit of Octopus Teacher or Back to the Future II on the big screen in the car for another 10 minutes.

Founded in 1948, FISITA is a global organization that brings together automotive engineering societies and industry experts to promote knowledge exchange and technological innovation in automotive engineering. It holds the World Mobility Summit every two years, bringing together executives and technology leaders from global mobility companies to discuss industry challenges and future technology directions, such as artificial intelligence (AI) and vehicle electrification .

This year’s summit is the first to be held in Korea . Chang Hwan Kim, Executive Vice President and Head of the Electrification Energy Solutions Tech Unit at Hyundai Motor Group, is the first Korean to serve as FISITA P resident .

“Hyundai Motor Group will continue to strengthen its competitiveness in key future mobility technologies and continue to participate in technology exchange and collaboration across the global automotive industry to contribute to the development of the future mobility sector.” –Chang Hwan Kim, Executive Vice President and Head of the Electrification Energy Solutions Tech Unit at Hyundai Motor Group

On the first day, Manfred Harrer, President and Head of R&D Division at Hyundai Motor Group, delivered a keynote address introducing the Group’s electrification strategy . It encompasses battery electric vehicles (BEVs), hybrid electric vehicles (HEVs), extended-range electric vehicles (EREVs) and fuel cell electric vehicles (FCEVs). Harrer described the Group’s technology development roadmap for responding flexibly to market changes and customer needs.

Harrer also emphasized strengthening future vehicle development capabilities by combining engineering technology with AI-based digital capabilities and connecting the strengths of different technologies to pursue a sustainable mobility future.

In his opening remarks, Kim said that the automotive industry is undergoing an unprecedented technological transition. He emphasized that diverse technology approaches and stronger global collaboration are important to the advancement of future mobility.

Under the theme “Embracing the Complexities of Mobility,” the summit is addressing key technologies and challenges facing the automotive industry, including software-defined vehicles (SDVs), AI, autonomous driving, batteries and energy infrastructure .

title: Two New Commissioners Headed to the Arizona Corporation Commission
raw_summary: Phoenix — Come January, the Arizona Corporation Commission (ACC) will be bi-partisan as two Democrats, Clara Pratte and Jonathon Hill, have been elected to the ACC. They will be joining current Republican commissioners Lea Márquez Peterson, Rachel Walden, and René Lopez. The election comes as the Commission is considering rate increases for Arizona Public Service Company (APS) and Tucson Electric Power Company (TEP), and mechanisms that would allow both utilities to increase rates every year with less stakeholder input, and as the Commission begins to consider the utilities’ proposed long-term resource plans. As a recent Sierra Club report makes clear, the ACC wields a tremendous amount of power over the future of Arizona’s energy landscape, public health, and utility bill increases, especially as the state experiences a fossil gas rush to power data centers. Arizonans experience some of the highest electric bills in the country, with some of the most planned gas in the country and with Arizona’s largest utility, APS, opting to run the dirty Four Corners coal plant for more than another decade. Yet, up until now, the Commission has made a habit of increasing ratepayer bills, opting for expensive fossil fuels and cutting programs that require utilities to utilize solar energy to generate electricity and to conserve energy, lower electric bills, and invest in energy efficiency.

article_paragraphs: Like many equipment brands, German forklift maker Jungheinrich has been struggling to crack the Asian industrial markets – but the company is set to change all that with the launch of a new line of 1.6- to 3-ton class electric forklifts designed specifically to navigate the region’s tight warehouses and factories.

Jungheinrich launched the next generation of its EFG MB and MC electric counterbalance forklifts, giving businesses more flexibility to match truck performance with the battery options, charging systems, and operator features that meet their specific needs .

“Different operations have different requirements,” said Lisa Jing Xue, Managing Director at Jungheinrich’s Qingpu Plant, China. “With the EFG M series, customers can configure the (forklift) truck around their application, workload and operators – whether they need greater maneuverability for confined warehouse spaces, or a stable, powerful truck for demanding transport and stacking work.”

Forklift buyers can choose between two performance packages, prioritizing energy efficiency for everyday material handling or more driving and lifting muscle for more demanding, high-throughput operations. The higher-performance package comes standard on models rated for 2.5-3.0 tons, with a choice of either lead-acid or lithium-ion batteries with 346 or 690 Ah of capacity available to suit different workloads and shift patterns. Both ship with regenerative braking tech that can recover up to 30% of the energy used in stopping and lowering loads , too, helping to keep these machines running longer between charging sessions.

“We carried out extensive customer research to understand what the market needs,” added Jing Xue. “Customers can invest in the performance required today and add further capabilities as their application demands.”

Optional features include fingertip controls, a larger 4″ digital display, upgraded LED lighting, and operator-assistance (ADAS) systems , while flexible seating and cabin configurations are designed to keep drivers comfortable through long shifts. A slim B-pillar and glass roof help visibility in busy warehouses , while the four-wheel EFG MC gets automatic cornering speed reduction as standard. Integrated telematics are also standard, giving fleet managers access to utilization data, maintenance planning and pre-operational checks from day one.

Jungheinrich says the order books for both the three- and four-wheel electric forklifts are open now, ready to be supported by the company’s 6,000+ person strong service network across the Asia-Pacific region.

article_paragraphs: Once America’s most popular electric pickup, the Ford F-150 Lightning is finding a second life on the used market.
The F-150 Lightning is hard to pass up at 50% to 60% off sticker price, even used. With new models no longer available , Ford’s electric pickup is suddenly selling like hotcakes on the used market.

After the last model rolled off the assembly line last December, CEO Jim Farley said the decision to end production came as the “very high-end EVs, the $50K, 70K, $80,000 vehicles, they just weren’t selling.”

At 50% to 60% off, it now looks like a bargain in the used market. “When Ford was selling it brand new, the math was complicated,” Jimmy Douglas, CEO of Plug, a wholesale EV dealer, recently told Bloomberg .
On the used market, however, “the Lightning is 50% to 60% of the sticker price and that is really a sweet spot,” he added.

Used Ford F-150 Lightnings are selling in about 20 days, less than half the 44-day average for used vehicles in the US. According to Edmunds.com , prices are now up 4% to about $50,000 since the start of the year.
Douglass said that close to one-third of used models are sold by rival dealerships that would normally flip them back to Ford. However, many are opting to sell them directly because of demand.
Chase Norris from Colorado called the electric pickup a bargain. He purchased a used Lightning for around $40,000 and considers it a major upgrade from his previous gas F-150.

article_paragraphs: Here's a better look at how BMW's new design language will look on its smallest electric SUV

Ushered in by the second-generation iX3 , BMW's Neue Klasse design philosophy abandons the brand's gargantuan front kidney grilles in favor of smaller ones, and an overall sleeker and more restrained design. Since the iX3, we've seen this new design language adopted by the i3, 7 Series, and the X5. Soon, the X2 will follow them into this new design era.

As we showed with spy shots back in July , all combustion-powered versions of the X2 are getting the new design. Now, for the first time, we can see the all-electric iX2 with these visual updates. Rather than an all-new generation, like the iX3, this new model is only a mid-cycle facelift, which explains why the overall shape and size of this updated model is virtually identical to the outgoing iX2.

BMW's designers have worked to overhaul the SUV's front fascia, incorporating the same small kidney grilles as other Neue Klasse models, as well as all-new headlights. One image shows the front turn signal enabled and previewing the LED daytime running light. While it's hard to say for sure, it looks like it adopts a V-shape. By comparison, the new iX3 DRLs are a diagonal slash, while the X5 has X-shaped light signatures .

BMW hasn't bothered tweaking the SUV's unflattering rear window and decklid spoiler, so the new iX2 still looks unnecessarily chunky. We can see there are new taillights, although the overall shape of them appears similar to the current model. What is different is the layout and shape of the LEDs, as they've been updated to better suit the Neue Klasse era. This being the electric iX2, there are obviously no tailpipes in sight.

These photos provide a glimpse of the iX2's updated interior. Like other Neue Klasse era models, we can see it includes BMW's new Panoramic iDrive system stretching across the width of the dashboard. It also has the same angular central infotainment display and will likely hit the market with the same odd four-spoke steering wheel as the iX3. Given the all-new interior layout, the updates made to the new iX2, and the combustion-powered X2 , will be substantial considering this is only a facelift.

With that being said, interested buyers shouldn't expect the new iX2 to debut with the latest-generation batteries and electric motors as the iX3. You see, while it will include the Neue Klasse design, it isn't expected to be based on the Neue Klasse platform and will use the current FAAR architecture. This new model will likely continue to be offered in eDrive20 and xDrive30 configurations, depending on the market. The first of those delivers 201 horsepower and 182 pound-feet of torque, while the xDrive30 has 308 hp and 364 lb-ft. Both share the same compact 66.5-kWh lithium-ion battery. BMW may choose to increase the same of the iX2's battery pack, though that's yet to be confirmed.

raw_title: Suzuki GSX-10R And SV-7S Put New Twists On Old Classics
title: Suzuki GSX-10R And SV-7S Put New Twists On Old Classics
raw_summary: Suzuki has long been, for better and for worse, a motorcycle maker that keeps its old assembly lines running. While the company comes up with something truly new every once in a while, it's more likely to figure out a new combination of parts it already has laying around . So, for EICMA , we shouldn't be surprised that Suzuki's big announcements are based around engines old enough to drink. We also shouldn't be surprised that those engines are inside what look to be some damn good bikes. Suzuki's big reveals this year are the SV-7S and GSX-10R, bikes built around the 27-year-old SV650 engine and 21-year-old K5 GSX-R1000 engines, respectively. The former looks to be a mild update to the outgoing SV650, with new lighting, emissions equipment, a quickshifter, and a ride-by-wire throttle wrapped around the prior bike's frame and engine. Most importantly, the SV-7S is available in Europe, meaning that the 645 cc V-twin lives on under Euro 5+ emissions. Suzuki's site doesn't list power claims for the new bike, but it's likely to make the same 73 horses it has since time immemorial.

Most importantly, the SV-7S is available in Europe, meaning that the 645 cc V-twin lives on under Euro 5+ emissions. Suzuki's site doesn't list power claims for the new bike, but it's likely to make the same 73 horses it has since time immemorial.

While the SV-7S is an update and a name change for the SV650, the GSX-10R (above) is ostensibly an entirely new bike — admittedly a bike that's largely just a faired version of the GSX-S1000, the company's naked literbike. Despite the similar displacement, the GSX-10R is nothing like the top-tier GSX-R1000. Instead, it's closer to a revival of the beloved K5 GSX-R1000 of the mid-aughts.

Yet, no matter what Reddit says, the GSX-10R is more than just a reheated leftover K5. Its name points to the difference, putting the bike in line with the GSX-8R — Suzuki intends the new 10R to be more streetable than the highest-test Gixxer, with lower footpegs, USB power, and a torque-rich engine for those times you can't sit at redline. There's also a full suite of electronics, to assist everything from traction to braking, launches, engine braking, hill starts, and cruising.

If the GSX-10R turns out to be what Suzuki says — a four-cylinder GSX-8R, a literbike with K5 reliability and daily-rider comfort — it could be the EICMA release I'm most excited to swing a leg over. To know for sure, though, I'll have to figure out how to get my hands on one.

article_paragraphs: Formula 1's 2026 title might already be officially decided, but that didn't prevent the first day of the Brazilian Grand Prix from being insightful.

George Russell is “a bit exhausted” from having to keep picking himself up after a disappointing 2026 season – and having reviewed the year with his team, he’s tallied up only six races without a problem.

The Mexican GP, where he started second but lost his chance of victory to a serious deployment issue on the run to the first corner, was the latest of the 14 races Russell says have been affected by factors outside of his control.

Retirements in Canada and Malaysia are headline examples, but he also had a significant setback in qualifying in China, lost big points with a drivethrough penalty in Monaco and had other engine-related issues hurt him in multiple grands prix - including Belgium where it dropped him into the pack and he crashed out after an incident with Lewis Hamilton.

Russell didn’t speak in the wake of his confirmed title defeat in Mexico a few days ago, where Kimi Antonelli sealed the championship. So Thursday at Interlagos was the first time to hear from him properly.
“When you get kicked to the ground, you pick yourself back up, then you get kicked down again, you pick yourself back up,” he said.
Half-joking, he added: “And I was hoping to do that maybe twice in the season, not every other weekend really!”

Despite the problems, and a lot of criticism being directed Mercedes’ way by his supporters, Russell insisted the team had not let him down, comparing this year’s fast but unreliable car with last year’s reliable one, which finished only fourth in the championship.

raw_summary: News about Honda making and selling new reproduction parts for the first-generation NSX has been brewing for more than a year now, but it's finally, actually here. The Honda Heritage Parts program launched in Japan back in April but is now making its way stateside. The automaker announced Monday that more than 3,000 Genuine Honda Reproduction Parts for its first-ever supercar are now available for purchase at Acura dealerships across the U.S. and via the online Honda DreamShop . There are apparently plans for "future expansion" of the program, as well. The American Honda Motor Co. hasn't released a master list of all 3,000 parts being offered, but taking a quick gander at the program's Japanese webpage shows a wide range of stuff available. You can get a camshaft for the yen equivalent of about $850, an accelerator pedal assembly costs $340, and the car's entire V6 cylinder block can be had for around $6,300. If you're a fan looking for some merch-type items, a little armrest emblem that says "NSX DOHC VTEC" on it and the Japanese NSX owner's manual go for about $40 and $60, respectively.

The O.G. NSX (known to Honda nerds as the NA1 and NA2) was branded in America as an Acura and was sold from model years 1991 to 2005, and the newly produced parts apply to NSXs across that entire production run. From Acura's press release: "Honda Heritage Parts was created to help our customers enjoy their classic Acura and Honda performance models, and it's appropriate that we begin with an iconic model like the first-generation Acura NSX," said American Honda executive vice president Mamadou Diallo (though the emphasis is mine). As the owner of a 2004 S2000 that could definitely use some rejuvenation here and there, hopefully that's the next Honda to get the Heritage Parts treatment.

article_paragraphs: Serve Robotics , a maker of self-driving sidewalk delivery robots, is expanding beyond its autonomous delivery operations in a bid to become a technology supplier to other companies building robots.
The company, which spun out of Uber’s acquisition of Postmates in 2021 and went public in 2024, said Thursday it will launch a new business line called Physical AI Services.

Specifically, Serve Robotics will offer customers its connectivity and data tools. Bedrock Robotics, a startup developing self-driving systems for construction equipment, is a customer, according to Serve. It’s also working with T-Mobile to bring AI computing power closer to robots, Serve announced alongside its third-quarter earnings on Thursday.
“We are solving the problem of robots in human spaces,” Serve Robotics CEO and co-founder Ali Kashani told TechCrunch.
Serve Robotics already makes two kinds of robots, the cute googly-eyed sidewalk delivery robot and one designed for hospitals that it got through its acquisition of Diligent Robotics .

Those businesses are not going away, Kashani emphasized in a recent interview. Instead, he said there is opportunity to sell the technology it developed for its own robots to other companies developing robots for farms, warehouses, and other uncontrolled environments.

“I kind of think of it as the AWS moment where we are taking the technology we’ve built for us, and we’re opening it up for more people to build on,” he said, adding this wouldn’t have been possible without developing its own robot fleet.
The expansion comes as Serve’s sidewalk delivery business expands, but is shifting away from Uber and toward other partners, including DoorDash and Wonder.

article_paragraphs: Harley-Davidson is one of the most famous names in motorcycling, but it's not one younger riders in the US have given much thought to for years. Its bikes are all too big, too heavy, and too expensive. Or they were until this week. This is the Sprint, an HD bike that costs just $6,000, and one you can actually pick up when it falls over, without hiring a crane.

The Sprint is Harley's long-awaited entry-level bike, and its mission is to attract a whole new generation of riders into the Harley gang. Rival brands like Royal Enfield and Triumph have been cleaning up with their small-capacity motorcycles, and HD wants a slice of that pie, with the hope that once the brand has got under a new rider's skin, they'll be a fan for life.

Design-wise, it's unmistakably Harley. Low seat, swept-back bars, heavily raked forks, and mag wheels. But it's shorter and, at just 412 lbs (187 kg) ready to ride, lighter than anything else in Harley's lineup by almost 100 lbs (220 kg).

Instead of a bubbly V-twin, the Sprint gets by with just one cylinder and 440 cc. It makes 27 hp (27 PS) and 28 lb-ft (38 Nm) of torque, which is funneled to the rear wheel via a six-speed manual transmission. Obviously it's going to sound very different to a traditional Harley, though engineers told MCN they'd purposely introduced some roughness to the way the engine runs to make it sound a bit more like a twin.

It certainly won't gobble gas like one. The tank holds only 2.4 US gallons (9.1), but combined with the claimed 80 mpg economy, that should be enough for most daily situations, plus the odd adventure.

Standard equipment includes a 3.5-inch display, LED lighting, and ABS, plus riders get to customize their bike by adding various options like throw-over saddlebags, a solo seat, and a clear windshield. Though that will, of course, take you further away from the $6,000 entry point that probably hooked you in in the first place.

Bike geeks might know that the Sprint borrows its name from a series of single-cylinder cycles Harley-Davidson sold in the 1960s, when it was attempting to fend off Honda. HD bought a 50 percent stake in Italian company Aermacchi, and started selling 18 hp sports bikes in the US that looked nothing like anything else you could buy from a Harley dealer at the time.

And if you know that, you might know that the 2027 Sprint isn't 100 percent new. It has its roots in another affordable motorcycle, the X440 made by India's Hero MotorCorp , and sold with Harley badges in Asia. The Sprint has been adapted to suit Western tastes, and it's also assembled in HD's Pennsylvania plant, though Harley stops short of claiming it's built there.

Or they were until this week.

It's deactivating all 61 of its Flock license plate readers by October 30. A few days later, it plans to verify that the shutdown actually worked.
article_paragraphs: It's no secret that Flock Safety is under fire. Sure, plenty of cities are pulling the plug and swapping in a different brand of plate reader, but Alexandria, Virginia, is different. It's deactivating all 61 of its Flock license plate readers by October 30. A few days later, it plans to verify that the shutdown actually worked. Recent events in Minnesota suggest that's a step well worth taking.

According to FOX 5 DC , Police Chief Tarrick McGuire told city leaders that Flock knows its time in Alexandria is coming to an end. The shift comes after a wave of backlash regarding privacy and access to vehicle-location data. Once the shutdown is over, the department plans to audit the cameras on November 2. That's key because the end of a Flock contract hasn't always meant that the ALPRs shut off. We'll circle back to that shortly.

Police in Alexandria say data connected to active investigations won't go away, but they'll remove user access by December 1. Interestingly, the department also plans to physically remove the cameras in the last month of the year as well. That's key because it's not as if officers don't appreciate the power afforded by these cameras.

The department has previously credited the technology with helping recover stolen cars and locate missing people. Its published accounting attributes 35 stolen-vehicle recoveries, four firearm recoveries, and three missing-person locations directly to license plate reader technology between August 1, 2025, and August 31, 2026.

As we've covered plenty of times, police can search far more than just a license plate. They can review cars by make, model, color, and even tiny details like bumper stickers and unique dents and damage. That wide-ranging ability can help police develop a lead from a vague description. Of course, it also makes oversight of who searches, and why, a central part of the debate. A potentially larger issue is when Flock doesn't actually follow the order of police .

As The Drive reports, Dayton, Minnesota, voted to end its Flock program in August. In September, the city learned of a maintenance work order and told the company that the program was on hold and no work should proceed. Two cameras were nevertheless reinstalled and placed back into service without authorization, according to the city's account. Staff discovered the second location while checking for other reinstalled equipment.

Nearby Plymouth had its own problem. Police Chief Eric Fadden said that after receiving no response from Flock's corporate or legal teams for more than a week, he directed staff to disconnect the cameras' power cords. Flock told KARE 11 that it respected both cities' decisions and was working with them to remove the equipment.

In Virginia, the next surveillance discussion is scheduled for November 10. Officials plan to establish guidance covering oversight, transparency, audits, and community involvement. Future deployments will allegedly require council approval.

It has already been a big part of Kia’s comeback in China and is expected to become one of its best-selling EVs.
Kia appears to be preparing an updated version. A new EV5 model was recently spotted by ShortsCar in a South Korean parking garage without camouflage, and it’s expected to be the updated version.
You can see in the video that the design has changed quite a bit. Up front, the hood and headlights remain about the same, but new design elements like a black accent light are added.
It also features a unique bumper design, similar to that of the rugged EV5 WKNDR Concept Kia revealed last November at the Guangzhou Motor Show.

The biggest changes are inside, where the interior appears to be completely overhauled. Instead of the current large display screen spanning from the driver to the center, the new EV5 features a display that extends from the center to the passenger side.

There also appears to be an added slim display in front of the steering wheel. Since Hyundai has recently added a slim display to vehicles equipped with its Pleos infotainment system, the updated Kia EV5 is expected to feature the new setup.

A pair of images of this wild, bright Red Mist Metallic Corvette ZR1X were recently shared on social media, and while the car itself is striking, that's not what has got people talking. Instead, it's the fact that George Nunnally Chevrolet has slapped the American supercar with a staggering $400,000 markup . We get it, ZR1Xs have been trading hands for silly money in recent months , but we're not so sure the Corvette represents good value at this price point.

The ZR1X in question is a loaded-up Convertible with the 3LZ package, a Jet Black interior, and has an MSRP of $296,445. Add the $400,000 mark-up on top of that, and you're looking at a ZR1X that costs $696,445. In the window sticker, the dealer describes the markup as an "Exclusive Market Value Adjustment," and calls it a "Tier-1 Production Allocation, Extreme Exclusivity, and Hypercar Demand Premium." Use as many adjectives as you'd like, because there's no way to justify this kind of price.

The dealer also describes the ZR1X as being built in "strictly limited production quantities from Bowling Green Assembly, [and] market adjustments reflect authentic real-time secondary and primary market demand." Though it's true there's strong demand for the flagship, all-wheel drive Corvette, it isn't a special edition, and production isn't being strictly limited by the company.

A budget of $700,000 can buy you some pretty remarkable supercars in the United States. Cars that come to mind include the Lamborghini Revuelto, priced from a touch over $600,000, and the Ferrari 849 Testarossa that starts at approximately $565,000. Admittedly, the ZR1X offers similar performance to those two, but no Corvette could ever match the cachet of an Italian supercar.

George Nunnally Chevrolet's website doesn't currently have this Corvette ZR1X listed, although we're not sure why. For those who are legitimately in the market for a ZR1X, it's worth noting there's no guarantee this model will remain the C8 flagship until the all-new, C9-generation arrives. Last year, Corvette chief engineer Tony Roma said the ZR1X "is not the end of the story," prompting speculation a new model could sit above it. One possibility is for a future Corvette version to use the new 6.7-liter V8 and couple it with the same twin-turbo and hybrid all-wheel drive setup as the existing ZR1X.

The Fiat Punto debuted in 1993, as a replacement for the Uno. The second generation arrived in 1999, followed by the Grande Punto in 2005. The latter received two major facelifts in 2009 (Punto Evo) and 2012 (Punto), and remained in production until 2018, when it was discontinued without a direct successor.

In a recent interview with L'Automobile Magazine during the 2026 Paris Motor Show, Belloni said: "After the C segment, where Fiat will offer a direct competitor to the Dacia Striker, there's the B segment. A brand like Fiat absolutely must have a Punto in its range."

The newly appointed CEO of Fiat, Abarth, and Lancia, who served as Renault's Global Marketing Director between 2020 and 2026, acknowledged that abandoning the traditional hatchback segment handed rival automakers a free pass to dominate supermini sales across Europe:

"The discontinuation of the Punto left Renault with a clear path to establish the Clio. Add to that the discontinuation of the Ford Fiesta and the lack of a new Volkswagen Polo, and the Clio found itself alone in the market, achieving triple commercial success. It's high time we reclaimed this territory."
While Fiat is known for adopting a retro styling approach in models like the 500 and the Grande Panda, the next Punto will follow an entirely different direction.

Belloni gave the example of the sixth-generation Renault Clio, saying that " such a radical redesign " was only possible because there were no strong ties with the past: "it's simply a hatchback in the B-Segment, which allows for total freedom to reinvent it". We guess that Fiat could also start fresh with the new Punto, giving it a modern stance. That would separate it from the rest of the lineup, which is divided into 500-inspired and Panda-themed models.
A new Fiat Punto could also serve as a base for a future Abarth hot hatch, filling a gap in the segment after the recent demise of the Ford Fiesta ST and VW Polo GTI.

title: GM Patents Cars That Change Camber And Ride Height Before You Lose Traction
raw_summary: Grip is important, and GM is working to find new ways to increase that grip Cars are absolutely full of wildly impressive technology. Among some of the most overlooked bits of that tech are the components that go into stability and traction control. General Motors just patented a system that would take that to a whole other level. It looks at the road ahead, predicts when a vehicle might begin to pull in an unwanted direction, and then automatically adjusts its suspension and steering in real time to help the driver maintain control.
summary: Grip is important, and GM is working to find new ways to increase that grip Cars are absolutely full of wildly impressive technology. Among some of the most overlooked bits of that tech are the components that go into stability and traction control. General Motors just patented a system that would take that to a whole other level.
article_paragraphs: Grip is important, and GM is working to find new ways to increase that grip

Cars are absolutely full of wildly impressive technology. Among some of the most overlooked bits of that tech are the components that go into stability and traction control. General Motors just patented a system that would take that to a whole other level. It looks at the road ahead, predicts when a vehicle might begin to pull in an unwanted direction, and then automatically adjusts its suspension and steering in real time to help the driver maintain control.

The newly granted patent, US 12,780,181 B1 , published November 3, describes technology designed to combat what GM calls "traction steer." That's when differences in grip between the left and right tires cause a vehicle to pull or turn unexpectedly, particularly during acceleration or braking. GM thinks it can predict those situations before they happen and use adjustable ride height, active camber, and steer-by-wire technology to minimize their effects. Ensuring that the resulting behavior feels natural to a driver might be tough.

Figure one of the patent gives us the clearest visual interpretation of how this would work. It shows a sedan with a huge network of sensors and communication systems. In practice, the car would use a forward-facing camera to identify the shape of the road ahead. The vehicle would then compare that to digital mapping data and try to determine how the surface could affect stability.

An inertial measurement unit and steering rack force sensor would verify those predictions. As the system calculates all of this data in real time, it would continue to predict if the upcoming road surface would upset stability. If the system believes the vehicle could lose stability, it would begin making corrections before a traction-steer event happens. That's where this gets particularly fascinating.

Rather than simply relying on steering and braking input, GM wants to actively change how the vehicle distributes its weight. In effect, it wants to leverage whichever tires have the most traction through that shift. For example, the patent explains that raising the left side of the vehicle could transfer additional load to the right-side tires.

Raising the front suspension could similarly shift load toward the rear axle. Depending on the road conditions, the system could make individual adjustments at each corner to better balance available traction. Of course, we've all seen active suspensions before, just not used in this particular way. What's wilder is the camber and steer-by-wire situation.

Steer-by-wire tech has been around for decades, but it wasn't until the Tesla Cybertruck that it made its way into a production vehicle on American roads. It provides an advantage in that it offers a variable ratio to drivers. In other words, turning the wheel 30 degrees to the right at 80 mph will turn the physical wheels differently than it would at 15 mph. That single feature would allow GM to make small steering adjustments at the front or rear wheels to compensate for forces that would otherwise pull it off course.

article_paragraphs: This Santa Fe's unexpected sales spike provided a much-needed boost for Hyundai's October sales

Hyundai just recorded its best October ever in terms of sales, but as we take a closer look at which vehicles performed well, it shows interesting trends in what buyers are looking for. Not surprisingly, the three-row Santa Fe was the strongest performer, but what did stand out is that without this SUVs sizeable surge, Hyundai would have been looking at a sales decline rather than a record month.

According to Hyundai's sales report , the brand sold a record 73,452 vehicles in October, and it's currently sitting on 770,916 sales for the year — that's a 5% increase from October 2025 and a 3% gain year to date. Those figures are mostly for context because the Santa Fe alone accounted for a 52% increase with 17,959 units sold last month compared to 11,800 sales a year ago. In other words, taking the Sante Fe out of the equation away, and the rest of the lineup was down roughly 5% year over year in October.
The auto industry is a tough one, and Hyundai's October sales show how a single car can make a month look better. With that in mind, let's look at the flip side of Hyundai's offerings.

Bolstering the Santa Fe's strong October, the Elantra, Kona, and Palisade grew 17%, 21%, and 14%, respectively, but the brand's most popular product, the Tucson, was a flop for the month. As buyers wait for the redesigned 2027 Hyundai Tucson , sales numbers plummeted by 23% to 17,808. Once the all-new fifth-gen Tucson hits dealers, those sales numbers should rebound.

Things are a little more concerning for other models, though. Despite overall sales being up 49% on the year so far, the Ioniq 9 was down a whopping 47% in October, but it's a low-volume offering with less than 7,000 sales so far this year. Similarly, the Sonata, was down 29% last month even though its year-to-date sales are up 14%. Not surprisingly, the Santa Cruz continues its downfall with a drop of 16%, which partly explains why the brand is killing it off .

Of course, a record month is still a record month in the end. As you can see, Hyundai's lineup was all over the place in terms of sales last month, with some big losers and some big winners, but the brand has reason to be excited for the future. Its hybrid volume increased 20% and represented 29% of total sales. So far this year, hybrid sales are up a whopping 50%.

raw_title: Hyundai Patents Wheels That Can Close Their Own Spokes At Speed
title: Hyundai Patents Wheels That Can Close Their Own Spokes At Speed
raw_summary: The humble automotive wheel has long faced a compromise. Open spokes allow plenty of airflow to help cool the brakes and other components. Wheels with closed or mostly closed faces don't get that benefit, but they are considerably more aerodynamic. Now, Hyundai and Kia are working on a way to have both. Their latest patented wheel design features movable blades that can effectively seal the openings between spokes when improved aerodynamics matter most. The companies received US Patent 12,779,902 B2 on November 3, 2026, for a wheel that can switch between open and closed configurations. The underlying application was first published in June 2025, but the newly granted patent offers a potentially clever solution to an age-old engineering compromise. If the automaker can make the technology work in development, putting it into production could help drivers save fuel without committing to closed-face wheels or losing brake cooling.
summary: The humble automotive wheel has long faced a compromise. Open spokes allow plenty of airflow to help cool the brakes and other components. Wheels with closed or mostly closed faces don't get that benefit, but they are considerably more aerodynamic. Now, Hyundai and Kia are working on a way to have both.
article_paragraphs: The humble automotive wheel has long faced a compromise. Open spokes allow plenty of airflow to help cool the brakes and other components. Wheels with closed or mostly closed faces don't get that benefit, but they are considerably more aerodynamic. Now, Hyundai and Kia are working on a way to have both. Their latest patented wheel design features movable blades that can effectively seal the openings between spokes when improved aerodynamics matter most.

The companies received US Patent 12,779,902 B2 on November 3, 2026, for a wheel that can switch between open and closed configurations. The underlying application was first published in June 2025, but the newly granted patent offers a potentially clever solution to an age-old engineering compromise. If the automaker can make the technology work in development, putting it into production could help drivers save fuel without committing to closed-face wheels or losing brake cooling.

The basic concept is very simple here. The newly patented wheels have a separate assembly behind the conventional spokes. That assembly features a rotating central ring and several blades. When the ring rotates in one direction, it moves the blades into a position behind the openings between the fixed spokes. That shift effectively improves how slippery the wheel is in the wind. Then, when those blades go back and hide behind the spokes, the airflow can get back to the brakes for cooling.

To be clear, the structural spokes on the wheel do not move. The only thing moving within the wheel assembly is the ring and blades. Hyundai mentions more than one way to make that ring-and-blade assembly work. Those options include electric motors, hydraulics, or pneumatic actuators. The automaker also mentions a shape-memory alloy component that changes length when electronically activated.

That component pushes the internal assembly into its closed position. A spring or similar elastic mechanism then pulls it back when the actuator releases. Hyundai also describes a small control board mounted within the wheel to manage the system. If it wasn't obvious before, this wheel sounds very complex and probably very expensive to replace if something goes wrong.

All this complexity comes down to optimizing the wheel for whatever it's doing. At highway speeds, Hyundai estimates that wheels and tires account for approximately 25% of a vehicle's aerodynamic resistance. That's a huge amount of drag, so reducing it could increase range whether the vehicle is electric or not. Of course, permanently sealing those openings creates another problem. Brakes generate considerable heat, and restricting airflow makes cooling them more difficult.

That said, these wheels work well because on the highway, drivers typically aren't using their brakes constantly. As a result, they rarely get overly hot. In other places, say around town, or descending from a mountain, overheating brakes are far more likely. That's where being able to open the wheels up and cool the brakes and other components can really pay off.

For now, Hyundai isn't saying if the system would activate at a specific speed or exactly how much drag the system would eliminate. Frankly, the design could just end up on the shelf like plenty of other patents we've reported on . Still, the underlying idea seems like a reasonable one. Especially given that every automaker is interested in marginal gains where fuel economy and range are considered.

Ferrari felt that their battle crossed a line with team boss Vasseur telling Canal+ on Sunday evening that it was evidence of a "lack of respect" to Ferrari's employees.
The Race understands Vasseur is planning to sit Hamilton and Leclerc down together on Friday in Brazil to discuss the matter.
Vasseur spoke to both drivers individually after the race in Mexico, but he's planned a proper sit-down for Brazil when they're all in the same place.
Leclerc missed Thursday media day in Brazil after announcing the birth of his and his wife Alexandra's child on Wednesday, so a meeting earlier in the Brazil weekend wasn't possible.
With Leclerc absent, only Hamilton faced the media on Thursday, where he doubled down on his criticism of Leclerc.

The new engine packages were unveiled at SEMA and each comes with a matching controller kit, making engine swaps as easy as possible. Included in the lineup of new engines are a pair of monstrous supercharged 6.2-liter V8s that'll make you forget about some of the brand's recent missteps, most notably with the controversial, all-electric Dodge Charger Daytona.

Sitting atop the new family of crate engines is the Hellephant Super Stock engine package. The familiar Hemi 6.2-liter V8 has a 3.0-liter supercharger, a 3.02-inch pulley to increase boost, and a sizeable 105 mm throttle body to help it suck in air at an alarming rate. Compared to less engines, this one also has upgraded pistons, new injectors to support E85 fuel, forged steel connecting rods, and a forged steel crank. It delivers up to 1,025 horsepower and 945 pound-feet with E85 . The crate engine package also includes all the engine wiring, O2 sensors, the powertrain control module, accelerator pedal, and for models using an automatic transmission, the shifter and brake press switch.

If this extreme engine sounds like a little too much for you, Direct Connection is also selling a supercharged 6.2-liter Hemi V8 rated at 885 hp and 787 lb-ft, known as the Hellcrate Redeye. This model uses a smaller 2.7-liter twin-screw supercharger, a cast iron block, and is sold with the same wiring and PCM setup as the Hellephant.

The line-up of crate engines also includes four naturally aspirated options. Sitting at the base of the range is a 5.7-liter V8 offered in Street Strip and Super Stock configurations. Both versions deliver the same 385 hp and 417 lb-ft. What differentiates them? Well, the Super Stock version has Redeye valve springs, an SRT Hellcat oil pump, a larger SRT oil filter, and an SRT oil cooler.

Completing the line-up are a pair of 6.4-liter Hemi V8s rated at 485 hp and 475 lb-ft. They too are sold in Street Strip and Super Stock forms, with the latter adding Redeye valve springs, an SRT Hellcat oil pump, and SRT oil cooler. Direct Connection is also selling crate packages for its TorqueFlite 8HP90 automatic transmission. Shoppers who would rather change their own gears can order a Tremec manual gearbox.

Stellantis has showcased its line of new crate engines with a modified 1967 Plymouth GTX , which we've seen in the past. At the 2024 SEMA Show, this classic Mopar was fitted with an EV drivetrain from the 2024 Charger Daytona, but for this year's show, it returns to its roots with a potent Hellcrate Redeye engine package under the hood. Sales of Direct Connection's new crate engine packages will begin in the first quarter of 2027.

This is Frostwarden. The oddly named Ford is the most radical interpretation of a modern Bronco ever built, making the Raptor feel like a base model by comparison. This insane Bronco, unveiled at SEMA, will not hit the production line, though you can buy the engine that powers it directly from Ford. We're crossing our fingers that at least one Bronco owner builds their own version of this concept, perhaps with the same engine.

The Bronco Frostwarden's highlight is the powertrain. It debuts Ford's all-new Megazilla 2.0 V8. This is the most powerful crate engine Ford Racing has ever built and has almost double the power of the original Megazilla released in 2022. Like that engine, this new one displaces 7.3 liters, and now includes a stronger block, upgraded pistons, larger fuel injectors, and a new belt drive and damper. Most importantly, it's topped with a 3.0-liter Whipple supercharger. This monster of an engine has over 1,200 horsepower and more than 1,000 pound-feet of torque.

Ford's popular Jeep Wrangler rival was the obvious choice for debuting the new Megazilla 2.0. The company's team has created a special Bronco Arctic search-and-rescue off-roader capable of traversing almost any terrain, and having the power to back it up.

The Bronco Frostwarden sits much higher than a typical Bronco thanks to advanced portal axles and huge 42-inch mud-terrain tires. Its bodywork is similar to the Raptor, but Ford has made some changes. For example, the flared arches are different, ensuring there's enough space to accommodate the tires. Bilstein suspension plays an important role in the overall package, and the Bronco's exterior is adorned with special accessories, perfectly fit for a dramatic SEMA project like this.

A winch sits behind the new front bumper, and a large yellow LED light bar sits above the windshield. A steel roof rack doubles as a spare-wheel carrier, and steel cross members run alongside the pillars to keep occupants safe should the Bronco ever find itself on its roof. A bunch of accessories have been added, including recovery tracks, spare fuel canisters, and roof boxes.

You can't mistake the cabin of this one-off Bronco for a regular model, with the seats, door panels, and dashboard featuring new black and yellow upholstery. Ford has also fitted a new steering wheel with carbon fiber accents and a large Megazilla badge.

Speaking with Street Muscle Magazine , Ford Racing Parts Product Manager Michael Goodwin says he tasked his engineering team with creating a 1,200 hp engine based on the Megazilla's 7.3-liter platform, and this is what they came up with. Beyond the 7.3-liter mill now sporting a Whipple supercharger, it includes a custom camshaft, ARP 2000 head studs, aluminum heads, and Callies H-beam connecting rods. According to Goodwin, the engine is a "natural candidate for trucks and street rods," so expect to see many wild builds using this engine in the coming years. Bring it on.

article_paragraphs: Lewis Hamilton maintains Ferrari needs further talks to iron out its rules of engagement, backing claims Charles Leclerc races him harder than drivers from rival teams.

Hamilton and Leclerc came to blows on lap one of last weekend's race in Mexico with both drivers going off the track at Turn 4, which eventually handed Max Verstappen a golden opportunity to snatch away the win and costing Ferrari a possible 1-2 victory, instead the duo finishing second and fourth.

Hamilton was incensed by how hard Leclerc raced on the opening lap, only for the Monegasque to permanently stay ahead as he cut the track at Turn 4. Leclerc only received a five-second penalty for gaining a lasting advantage, with mitigation bringing that punishment down from 10 seconds.

Their Mexico fight further fed suggestions that Leclerc appears to race his teammate harder than anyone else, having come after a Singapore Grand Prix in which Leclerc backed off at the start despite being fully on the inside of polesitter Max Verstappen. Leclerc did race the Dutchman hard at the subsequent US Grand Prix in Austin, however, overtaking the Red Bull man around the outside of COTA's Esses.

When asked if the idea of Leclerc racing him harder than other drivers is something Hamilton has also noticed, the seven-time world champion replied: "Yes. I see what you see. In Singapore, he was fully on the inside into Turn 1, he had won the lead, and he backed off. It was definitely different.
"But I mean, if you look at the team-mates, it was the same with Sebastian [Vettel]. It was the same with Carlos [Sainz].

As emotions ran high, Hamilton demanded talks to clarify the team's rules of engagement and warned of "big problems" for the squad. Autosport understands team principal Fred Vasseur has spoken briefly to both drivers, albeit separately, after feeling the events of Mexico showed a lack of respect towards the team's 2000 people staff.

But with Vasseur having travelled back to Europe in between races and Leclerc spending time with his family following the birth of his daughter, Hamilton welcomes further talks with Leclerc and their boss in Sao Paulo on Friday. "Naturally I was frustrated, and I'm still frustrated," he said when asked by Autosport if he views the events of Mexico in a different light now they have had time to cool off. "So, conversations need to be had. We will have those when the time permits.

title: Urgent Safety Alert: Hyundai is recalling nearly 30,000 Kona Electric vehicles due to an airbag software defect
raw_summary: Hyundai issued a recall affecting nearly 30,000 Kona Electric vehicles due to a software error that could cause the airbag to fail to deploy in a crash. In a letter sent to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on November 4, Hyundai said it was recalling certain 2019 to 2023 Kona Electric and 2019 to 2022 Veloster N vehicles.
summary: Hyundai issued a recall affecting nearly 30,000 Kona Electric vehicles due to a software error that could cause the airbag to fail to deploy in a crash. In a letter sent to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on November 4, Hyundai said it was recalling certain 2019 to 2023 Kona Electric and 2019 to 2022 Veloster N vehicles.
article_paragraphs: Hyundai issued a recall affecting nearly 30,000 Kona Electric vehicles due to a software error that could cause the airbag to fail to deploy in a crash.
In a letter sent to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration on November 4, Hyundai said it was recalling certain 2019 to 2023 Kona Electric and 2019 to 2022 Veloster N vehicles.
The recall impacts 37,901 vehicles in total, including 29,058 Kona Electric and 8,843 Veloster N models.

According to documents submitted to the NHTSA, the issue stems from a software error with the airbag control unit (ACU) that can cause the airbag malfunction indicator light (MIL) to come on and the airbag system to deactivate under certain driving conditions.
The data may become corrupted during a system reboot or power interruption while the system is writing to the ACU’s memory. When this happens, the airbag MIL will illuminate to warn drivers.
As of October 22, 2026, Hyundai is aware of 331 alleged incidents related to the issue. However, none have resulted in a crash, fire, or injury.
Owners can take their vehicle to the closest dealer, where it will update the ACU software, free of charge.

Hyundai expects to mail out owner notification letters on January 1, 2027. In the meantime, owners can contact Hyundai’s customer service at 1-855-371-9460 with any questions or concerns. Hyundai’s recall number is 311.
