article_paragraphs: Panamera sales dropped 38 percent this year, but Porsche hopes a MY28 update can get it back on track

Some brands lurch from one styling trend to another, all smooth curves one minute, and boxy shapes and angles the next. Porsche isn't one of those brands. Its design philosophy evolves so slowly it makes the glaciers that formed the mountains of the Alps look fast moving. It's why the profile of today's 911 is almost exactly the same as the first one's 63 years ago, and why the changes to this Panamera prototype spotted testing at the Nürburgring are incredibly hard to spot.

The Panamera is Porsche's gasoline- and hybrid-powered sedan, an ICE companion to the electric Taycan, and was heavily overhauled for 2024. But it's been back on the surgeon's table for some more tweaking. Spy photographers snapped the sporty GTS version last month, and now we're getting a look at two of the lower trims levels, one straight gas, one hybrid, in a set of really clear images that show the sedans wearing zero disguise. That lack of camo suggests a debut is imminent for MY28.

You really have to look closely to tell the two apart though, from the front, at least, even without disguise. The headlights and daytime running lights (DRLs) are identical, and even the basic bumper shape is only slightly different. The most notable change between the two is that the diagonal element becomes a horizontal bar on the base car, rather then a fatter, vertical one, as seen on the GTS. We've included a picture above so you can see what we're talking about, but be prepared to zoom in.

Porsche has made our job a little easier at the back. The GTS has an aggressive rear bumper with a large vent on each side, but the more affordable Panamera hybrid in these new shots (you can just make out the charging flap on the left fender) goes for a narrower, more minimalist look.

Both the hybrid and GTS prototypes have two pairs of round tailpipes, though we think the base car must be fitted with an optional sports exhaust, otherwise it'd have two pipes. But there are subtle differences in the way the rear undertray merges into the bumper. The hybrid's lower bumper is mostly smooth, while the GTS makes a vague attempt to look more like a diffuser. Both look sportier than before. Just don't bank on those new parts producing much meaningful downforce.

Elsewhere on the rear end, a long, narrow strip of LED taillights runs across the tail as on the current car, and Porsche's R&D team has taped over the illuminated "PORSCHE" lettering introduced for 2024. Overall, there's not much to tell the new car from the old.

And it's likely that the engine lineup won't be radically different either. Today's entry-level Panamera comes with a 3.0-turbocharged V6 that makes 348 hp (350 PS), the 4 E-Hybrid also gets a 3.0-turbocharged V6, but it pumps out 463 hp (469 PS), and the 4S E-Hybrid makes 536 hp (543 PS).

Under the new partnership announced Thursday, Amazon Prime members will be able to order food from Uber Eats directly through Amazon.com and the Amazon Shopping app. Importantly, Prime members won’t need to create an Uber account and won’t pay a delivery fee on orders of more than $25, the companies said. article_paragraphs: Amazon has made Uber Eats its official restaurant delivery partner for Prime members in the United States, effectively ending the e-commerce giant’s existing deal with Grubhub. Under the new partnership announced Thursday, Amazon Prime members will be able to order food from Uber Eats directly through Amazon.com and the Amazon Shopping app. Importantly, Prime members won’t need to create an Uber account and won’t pay a delivery fee on orders of more than $25, the companies said.

Amazon’s commercial agreement with Grubhub that gave Prime members access to Grubhub+ ends Thursday, according to an Amazon spokesperson, who said the company continuously evaluates its third-party offers. Amazon said it identified an opportunity to deliver an even better restaurant delivery experience.

A Grubhub spokesperson also confirmed the agreement was ending. Prime members can no longer place orders through Amazon.com or the shopping app However, if Prime members had already activated Grubhub+, they will still be able to use that membership through December 31, 2027.

The new partnership deepens an already extensive relationship between Amazon and Uber. The companies have existing agreements spanning cloud computing, Zoox robotaxis, and the integration of Uber Eats into Amazon’s AI-powered Alexa+ assistant .

It also allows Amazon to give its Prime members another sweetener to justify that annual membership fee. To help kickstart the initiative, Amazon and Uber are offering Prime members $20 off their first two orders of $25 or more during the first two weeks.
Amazon’s ouster of Grubhub ends a once-close relationship. Amazon first struck a deal with the company in 2022 , offering Prime members a free Grubhub+ subscription.

Two years later, Amazon expanded its commercial agreement and made the free Grubhub+ membership an ongoing offer for Prime members. The e-commerce giant also reached a deal with Grubhub’s then-owner, Just Eat Takeaway.com, to increase its equity stake in the food delivery company to as much as 18%.

Under that performance-based agreement, which was set to renew annually, Amazon could receive warrants representing an additional stake in Grubhub. But just months later, Just Eat Takeaway announced plans to sell Grubhub to Wonder. According to Just Eat Takeway’s annual report, Amazon in December 2024 elected to cash out on its outstanding exercisable warrants.

title: The Olds Calais Was An Indy 500 Pace Car Edition With No Pace
raw_summary: For as long as there's been an Indianapolis 500, there's been an Indianapolis 500 pace car. But it took until 1953 — 42 years after the inaugural race — for automakers to realize they could make bank by peddling replicas of the sedans, coupes and convertibles that led the field. Some of these lookalikes, cars like the orange and white 1969 Chevy Camaro SS/RS, and the the black and silver 1978 Corvette pace car replica , are blue-chip collector classics. Others, like this Oldsmobile Calais 500 , which is up for auction through Bring a Trailer, are rarely remembered. Oldsmobile reportedly built 2,998 Calais 500 commemorative pace car editions (confusingly, some sources say just 242), though none of them looked anything like the real version. The genuine Indy Calais driven by Rockford Files star James Garner, (there were actually two cars) was a special convertible version that Olds never offered to the public.
summary: For as long as there's been an Indianapolis 500, there's been an Indianapolis 500 pace car. But it took until 1953 — 42 years after the inaugural race — for automakers to realize they could make bank by peddling replicas of the sedans, coupes and convertibles that led the field.
article_paragraphs: For as long as there's been an Indianapolis 500, there's been an Indianapolis 500 pace car. But it took until 1953 — 42 years after the inaugural race — for automakers to realize they could make bank by peddling replicas of the sedans, coupes and convertibles that led the field. Some of these lookalikes, cars like the orange and white 1969 Chevy Camaro SS/RS, and the the black and silver 1978 Corvette pace car replica , are blue-chip collector classics. Others, like this Oldsmobile Calais 500 , which is up for auction through Bring a Trailer, are rarely remembered.

Oldsmobile reportedly built 2,998 Calais 500 commemorative pace car editions (confusingly, some sources say just 242), though none of them looked anything like the real version. The genuine Indy Calais driven by Rockford Files star James Garner, (there were actually two cars) was a special convertible version that Olds never offered to the public.

Also not available via your Oldsmobile dealer, was the real pace car's specially tuned 2.7-liter version of GM's 2.5-liter Tech-4 inline-4 that whipped up 215 horsepower to ensure it could stay ahead of the open-wheel Indy racers.

The Calais was new for 1985, and shared its front-wheel drive N-body platform with the Pontiac Grand Am and Buick Somerset Regal. It came with either two or four doors, both with a vertical back window style lifted from Olds' bigger cars, a hangover from the 1970s that looked about as modern as cycle fenders and wooden spoked wheels.

All pace car editions got the two-door body, and came dressed in red metallic paint with a silver lower body, silver pace car graphics plastered across the doors, plus another sticker on the tail, and a couple of badges. They also got a silver and red bucket seat interior that made the car look like it was built to celebrate a NASA launch, not an automobile race. And, after that, Oldsmobile seems to have run out of ideas.

There were no mechanical upgrades, and you could even order your Calais 500 pace car edition with that year's standard Calais engine, the 92-horsepower 2.5-liter inline-4. Maybe the 500 referred to its 0-60 mph time. Salvation of sorts came in the form of an optional 3.0-liter V6, which pushed out 125 hp, though that meant forgoing a five-speed manual option, and putting up with a three-speed automatic.

Motorweek took a Calais V6 from zero to 60 mph in 11.4 seconds, performance it described as "commendable." Which just shows how easily pleased reviewers were back then, after having endured a decade of cars with smog-choked motors.

This auction Calais 500 is one of what the owner claims were 600 cars ordered with the 3.0-liter V6, and shows just 13,000 miles. Its silver interior looks virtually untouched, and the exterior is pretty peachy, too. Only the grubby engine and deteriorated hood insulation lets the the look down. Our favorite detail besides that upholstery has to be the Auto-Calculator trip computer, which must have seemed incredibly trick back in 1985.

The Limo uses the familiar 2.4-litre four-cylinder diesel engine which is coupled with a manual transmission. The regular Innova Crysta has a certified fuel-efficiency figure of up to 15 kmpl. article_paragraphs: Strong like an ox, psychologically more airtight than anyone who's ever climbed into a race car, and the most aggressive wheel-to-wheel racer who scared the living daylights out of his rivals.

Little wonder Alan Jones - who has died, aged 80 - became an archetype of the perfect racing driver for Frank Williams and Patrick Head as they jointly put the Williams team on the map out of nowhere. It was a status they formalised by winning the 1980 drivers' and constructors' world titles together.
He wasn't particularly rated as an obvious world champion when he came over to the UK from Australia with £50 in his back pocket, to race in F3 in 1970.
But he was a hefty guy in an under-powered formula and still he was a frontrunner for a few seasons in British F3 and Formula Atlantic.
His first F1 chance came in 1975, with Graham Hill's team and a subsequent ride in Harry Stiller's privateer Hesketh.

He showed enough for John Surtees to take him on for the '76 season. At the non-championship Race of Champions he foreshadowed his later form by leading and dicing with James Hunt's McLaren but it was a low-key season and Jones and Surtees, as two hard-headed individuals dissatisfied with their situation, didn't hit it off. Jones left at the end of the season, prepared to walk out of F1 rather than stay in that environment.
Which made him available four races into the '77 season as a short-notice replacement at Shadow after Tom Pryce's fatal accident in the South African Grand Prix.

The Shadow DN8 was a little overweight but well-balanced enough for Jones' talent to become apparent. His victory in the wet Austrian Grand Prix was something of a shock result but he was quick, consistent and combative all year.

summary: Hyundai Motor India has introduced a Usage-Based Insurance (UBI) programme for eligible customers with Bluelink-connected vehicles . article_paragraphs: Hyundai Motor India has introduced a Usage-Based Insurance (UBI) programme for eligible customers with Bluelink-connected vehicles . Announced in association with partner insurers, the initiative could help customers save on their insurance renewal premium based on their driving behaviour.

The programme uses vehicle data recorded through Bluelink to generate a personalised driving score. This score is calculated using driving behaviour from the previous three months, assessing parameters such as rapid acceleration, rapid deceleration, braking, speed control and idling.

Since the information comes directly from the connected vehicle, customers do not need to install an additional tracking device. They can view their UBI score, check eligibility and choose whether to share the score with participating insurers through the Bluelink app.

Hyundai India Insurance Broking (HIIB) will act as an intermediary, facilitating the sharing of customer-consented driving scores between Hyundai and the insurance partners. Insurers will then use the score during underwriting to determine potential benefits at policy renewal.

Customers whose insurance renewal is due within the next 90 days will be able to view their score and explore potential insurance benefits. A UBI score of 70 or above may qualify for benefits, subject to the insurer’s underwriting policy and conditions.

Customers with scores below the threshold can use personalised driving tips to improve their driving behaviour and potentially become eligible for benefits. However, Hyundai has not disclosed a detailed score-to-discount structure.

The potential saving applies specifically to the own-damage premium. It should therefore not be interpreted as a flat 15% reduction in the total insurance bill. The release also does not specify whether a lower driving score could affect the renewal quote.

The initial phase includes Cholamandalam MS General Insurance, Go Digit General Insurance and ICICI Lombard General Insurance. The programme will be available to eligible customers across Hyundai’s Bluelink-connected product portfolio, with upcoming insurance renewals falling within the eligibility window.
